entities.name: Major neurocognitive disorder
observations: Cognitive decline that interferes with independence, especially complex instrumental activities, supports major neurocognitive disorder despite preserved basic activities of daily living.
In this case, dependence for driving, medications, meals, and finances supports major neurocognitive disorder rather than pure mild cognitive impairment.

entities.name: Mild cognitive impairment
observations: Mild cognitive impairment requires objective cognitive decline with essentially preserved functional independence; meaningful instrumental activity dependence argues against a pure MCI diagnosis.

entities.name: Alzheimer disease
observations: Progressive memory-predominant cognitive decline with executive dysfunction in an older adult, after unrevealing depression, laboratory, and MRI evaluation, is clinically suggestive of early Alzheimer disease causing major neurocognitive disorder.
Normal structural MRI does not exclude early Alzheimer disease; clinical data suggest but do not biologically confirm the etiology.
